rules.rule_text: name: 1-64 characters, lowercase letters, digits and hyphens only; no leading or trailing hyphen, no consecutive hyphens; it must match the skill folder name.
name must not contain XML tags or the reserved words "anthropic" or "claude".
Prefer a gerund name describing the activity (processing-pdfs, analyzing-spreadsheets); avoid vague names like helper, utils, tools, data.
description: non-empty, at most 1024 characters, no XML tags.
description says both what the skill does and when to use it ("Use when ..."), in the third person, with the concrete keywords, file types and phrases a user would actually say.
If the skill could trigger on unrelated requests, add negative triggers ("Do NOT use for ...") and narrow the scope.
Put the main use case first: Claude Code truncates description plus when_to_use to 1,536 characters in the skill listing.
A portable skill uses only the standard frontmatter keys: name, description, license, compatibility, metadata, allowed-tools.
Keep the SKILL.md body under 500 lines and concise: Claude is already smart, so explain only what it does not know.
Give one default approach for the common case, with at most one fallback, instead of a menu of options.
For multi-step tasks, give a checklist Claude copies and ticks off, with a validate-fix-repeat loop before moving on.
Match the degree of freedom to fragility: prose for open tasks, templates for preferred patterns, exact commands for fragile operations.
Use one consistent term per concept and no time-sensitive instructions.
Move detail into files referenced one level deep from SKILL.md (references/, scripts/, assets/), with forward-slash paths.
Say explicitly whether Claude should run a script or read it as reference; scripts handle their own errors and list dependencies.
Never put API keys, passwords or tokens in skill files.
Put the rules whose breach ruins the result near the top of the body, right after Quick start: after context compaction only the start of a skill may be kept.
The body stays in context and is not re-read, so write guidance that holds for the whole task as a standing instruction ("Run the tests after every edit"), not a one-time step.
Give a rule whose purpose is not obvious its reason in a few words instead of a bare MUST: a model that knows why applies the rule to cases the text did not foresee.
For batch, destructive or irreversible operations use plan-validate-execute: analyze, write the plan, validate the plan, execute, verify.
A sequential workflow states the step order, what a step takes from an earlier one, a check at each stage, and what to do when a step fails (stop, roll back, report).
When the work branches, name the decision point first and send each case to its own short workflow ("Creating new content? Follow the creation workflow.").
Give the output a template and match its strictness to the need: "use exactly this structure" for data formats, "a sensible default, adapt as needed" otherwise.
When output quality depends on style, give 2-3 input -> output pairs: examples show the style and level of detail better than descriptions.
In Claude Code, ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} expands to the folder of SKILL.md; elsewhere use paths relative to SKILL.md.
